The United States Space Force (USSF) Civilian Talent Management Office (CTMO) at Joint Base San Antonio, Texas is searching for Human Resources Information Systems Specialist (NH-0201-03, GS 12/13 equivalent). Description: As a Human Resources Specialist for the U.S.

Space Force, you will serve as a technical expert and data innovator at the heart of the Civilian Talent Management Office, shaping how the service builds its elite workforce.

In this dynamic role, you will lead challenging projects to design, analyze, and automate critical human capital processes by harnessing the power of advanced data systems like PowerBI, Business Objects (BOXi), Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), Manpower Programming and Execution System (MPES), myFSS, USA Staffing, and PowerApps.

By transforming raw HR data into actionable intelligence, you will create sophisticated reports, deliver high-impact briefings to senior Space Force leaders, and develop innovative solutions to complex organizational challenges, ensuring that the USSF can recruit, hire, and retain the nation's top talent.

If you are a proactive problem-solver with a passion for data and a drive to build the workforce of the future, apply today to make your mark on the newest branch of the armed forces.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned and proactive Human Resources data expert with a proven mastery of federal HR information systems, particularly PowerBI, Business Objects (BOXi), Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS), Manpower Programming and Execution System (MPES), myFSS, USA Staffing, and PowerApps.

This individual possesses an innate ability to not only extract and manipulate complex datasets but also to conduct deep-dive analyses, turning raw data into actionable intelligence and strategic recommendations for senior leadership.

As a natural problem-solver and leader, they are adept at independently managing projects, developing automated solutions for HR processes, and mentoring junior team members.

Their exceptional communication skills allow them to translate highly technical information into clear, compelling briefings and to build strong collaborative relationships across various DAF, Field Command, and installation organizations.

Ultimately, this professional is a forward-thinking innovator who combines deep knowledge of federal HR principles with advanced technical skill to drive data-centric decision-making and enhance the operational effectiveness of the U.S. Space Force. Key Skills and Abilities: 1.

Knowledge of a wide range of federal Human Resources (HR) laws, executive orders, regulations, policies, directives, instructions, and concepts governing HR functions. 2.

Knowledge of advanced federal human resources management (HRM) principles, concepts, practices, fact finding and analytical methods, a wide range of qualitative and quantitative techniques, and relationships of various HR disciplines as well as seasoned consultative skill sufficient to resolve complex HRM problems not susceptible to treatment by standard methods. 3.

Knowledge of databases, higher-order programming tools and retrieval languages associated with the HR information system(s) and system capabilities, procedures, limitations and retrieval options. 4. Knowledge of organizational structures, missions, objectives, operating programs, key positions, and administrative/protocol policies and procedures. 5.

Skill in conducting reviews and analyzing and assessing HR data analytics to include identifying deficiencies; measuring compliance, consistency, and effectiveness; and making recommendations for enhancements and improvements. 6.

Ability to communicate both orally and in writing and to establish and maintain effective and positive working relationships.

People Operations is the operational engine of the People function at Cint.
Our mission is to build a scalable, intelligent and employee-centric operating model that enables the business to grow without increasing complexity. We achieve this by combining exceptional operational excellence with technology, automation and AI.

Most People Operations functions are still built for yesterday's world. We intend to build one for tomorrow.
This role will lead that transformation.
You will work closely with People Technology, Employee Relations, People Partners, Talent Teams, Total Rewards, Payroll, IT and Legal. You'll lead the evolution of our global People Operations function, combining operational excellence, technology, automation and AI to build a service that is fast, intelligent and ready for the future.

This position will be assigned to the Human Resources Information Systems Branch within the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC). The primary purpose of this position is ensuring continuous and efficient operations of automated human resources (HR) personnel systems.

The incumbent of this position assumes a key role in implementing initiatives that work towards improving HR automated systems and applications. Manages the functional operations of HR automated systems and applications. Advises on the carrying out of system enhancements for automated systems and applications.

Interprets system requirements needed for proposed system changes. Gauges system supportability and considers the impact on HR processes, then makes recommendations. Identifies procedures impacted by system changes, and provides recommendations which correspond with system changes and continue to meet applicable laws and policies.

Functions as a project manager in the transition from a legacy automated system to a new/upgraded automated system. Prepares a business case on proposed automated system(s). Develops business case studies that outline costs and benefits. Functions as a business partner with other agencies.

Considers the impact across divisions and ensures stakeholders are aware of and prepared for the system transition. Establishes an implementation/transition plan with timelines and milestones. Meets timeline accomplishment through various phases from development through production and deployment.

Incorporates a plan to pilot the system during the transition phase. Identifies pilot team(s), which may include individuals from various offices or an entire office. Initiates and maintains strategic communications during all phases of implementation. Generates a plan to train personnel on the automated system, if needed.

Ensures milestones are met or extensions are granted. Maintains personnel automated systems. Resolves system Remedy tickets. Provides information on system updates/enhancements. Distributes notifications when scheduled system updates occur. Notifies servicing offices of changes in procedures due to system errors. Determines user permission profiles.

Develops processes for system access. Creates and maintains user accounts. Assists users with obtaining appropriate account-level access. Deletes/retires user accounts. Performs random and/or scheduled quality control checks. Conducts training for HR personnel on all automated HR systems and applications. Generates random and/or scheduled reports.

Reviews data from reports for compliance with HR policies and procedures. Works with individuals in correcting errors. Provides feedback on areas that may require additional training based on a consistent pattern of findings. Performs additional duties as assigned.

As a Human Resources Specialist (Employee Benefits) at the GS-0201-13 level, the incumbent will be part of the Office of Human Resources, Office of the Managing Director, Federal Maritime Commission.

The incumbent This position is responsible for administering the employee benefits program, which includes retirement, health insurance, life insurance, thrift savings plans, and Workers' Compensation Program.

As an HR Specialist (Employee Benefits), if selected, you will: Develops and conducts new employee orientation and participates in onboarding.

Ensures that new employees are appropriately entered on the agency rolls, counseled, and that all necessary actions related to benefits, obtaining information from prior Federal employment, employee rights and responsibilities, pay, etc. have been completed. Ensures proper completion of forms and follow up on due dates.

Provides customized expert counseling and guidance to all levels of employees on matters of a highly sensitive/serious nature, relating to the areas of retirement, which can include retirement (CSRS/FERS), health, life, and long-term care insurance, thrift savings plans, Flexible Spending Accounts, death and survivor benefits, debt and overpayments, Work Life, workers' compensation, telework, and leave administration, as well as the use of the Employee Personal Page (EPP) self-servicing system.

Counsels employees concerning service credit payments and post-1956 military service deposits. Assists employees with applications for retirement and verifies credibility of service. Provides employees and survivors of deceased employees estimates of expected benefits.

Assists managers in making proper referrals to external resources for employees with highly personal and/or controversial problems, e.g., contested disability retirements. Identifies appropriate sources of training for FMC employees in the areas of benefits, retirement, and financial literacy.

Arranges and/or conducts training to be presented to employees and develops metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of the training. Provides advice on benefits procedures, forms, eligibility requirements, and coverage. Computes benefits and processes actions to completion, advising appropriate agency staff of pending actions.

Coordinates open seasons and enrollment periods for benefits and prepares and distributes guidance and relevant materials. Organizes the annual FMC Employee Benefits Fair held during open season.

Prepares retirement estimates utilizing an automated retirement system (such as FedHR Navigator); prepares retirement packages, ensuring accuracy/completeness, and submits to NFC for processing. Prepares the FMC's Annual Employee Financial Education Plan for submission to OPM.

Identifies strategies to help the Commission improve employee financial literacy and retirement readiness.

Skill and ability to analyze and solve particularly complex and sensitive problems and issues, such as those involving apparently conflicting laws or other requirements and those involving vague or untested areas of case law.

Qualifying specialized experience includes: experience in executing, directing, and/or managing the delivery of federal civilian human resources (HR) services involving multiple of the following functions - recruitment and placement, position management and classification, compensation, employee relations, labor relations, equal employment opportunity, employee benefits, oversight of automated personnel information systems and employee development; ensuring compliance with governing laws and regulations; developing, interpreting, and/or advising senior management on HR policies and administration; providing substantive input to the strategic planning of human capital resources for an organization.

Das Personalamt des Kantons Zürich ist zuständig für alle personal-, arbeits- und sozialversicherungsrechtlichen Fragen der über 30'000 Mitarbeitenden des Kantons Zürich. Du bringst Themen ins Rollen, verbindest die richtigen Menschen und machst aus Konzepten gelebte Praxis. Dabei begleitest du Veränderungsprozesse und Teamentwicklungen und bringst deine Expertise in Führung und Organisation ein.

### Deine Aufgaben ###
* Du führst neue HR-Instrumente und Führungsprozesse in der Finanzdirektion ein und begleitest sie bis in die praktische Anwendung - beispielsweise bei Mitarbeitendenbefragungen, Führungsentwicklung oder Nachfolgeplanung.

### Dein Profil ###
* Du verfügst über einen Hochschulabschluss in HR Management, Personal- oder Organisationspsychologie oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.

* Du denkst analytisch und konzeptionell, behältst auch bei komplexen Fragestellungen den Überblick und entwickelst praxistaugliche Lösungen.
* Du verfügst über eine hohe Beratungs- und Kommunikationskompetenz, moderierst sicher und schaffst es, unterschiedliche Anspruchsgruppen und Perspektiven einzubeziehen.
* Moderne HR-Instrumente und aktuelle HR-Trends sind dir vertraut und du interessierst dich für neue Ansätze.
### Unser Angebot ###
* Unser HR-Umfeld ist im Wandel. Ideal, wenn du gerne mitdenkst, mitgestaltest und Neues mit auf den Weg bringst.
* Flexible Arbeitszeiten, Homeoffice-Möglichkeiten und eine faire Entlöhnung sind bei uns selbstverständlich.

This role goes beyond operational HR support you will influence leadership capability, organisational design, talent strategy, and culture in a fast-moving fintech environment. You will balance commercial acumen with people expertise to ensure our teams can perform at their best while building a sustainable, inclusive and high-performing culture.

Strategic People Partnership
Partner with senior leaders to translate business objectives into actionable People strategies.
Act as a trusted advisor and coach to leaders, driving accountability and high performance.
Talent Strategy & Workforce Planning
Drive and take ownership of the workforce planning and support the Talent Acquisition team to shape hiring plans aligned to business growth and skills needs.
You will play an active role in supporting recruitment through coaching hiring managers to elevate hiring standards and ensure consistent, high-quality selection processes.
Proactively identify capability gaps and future talent risks within Product Engineering and Operations.
Performance & High-Performance Culture
Lead performance management cycles, ensuring robust goal setting, feedback, calibration, and development planning is in operation and meeting our standards.
Enable managers to confidently manage both high and low performance.
Embed a culture of continuous feedback, accountability, and growth.
Leadership & Capability Development
Diagnose development needs across teams and implement targeted learning initiatives.
Coach managers to strengthen leadership capability, employee engagement, and team effectiveness.
Support succession planning and internal mobility strategies.
Employee Relations & Risk Management
Serve as a trusted advisor and manager all employee relations matters within your functions and support others when and where appropriate.
Provide balanced, commercially sound guidance that mitigates risk while maintaining trust.
Ensure People practices align with employment law and regulatory requirements whilst staying in line with our people centric approach.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
Embed inclusive leadership practices across Product Engineering and Operations.
Partner with leaders to drive equitable talent outcomes across hiring, performance, and progression.
Use data insights to identify and address systemic gaps.
Engagement & Culture
Translate engagement data into actionable insights and support with driving measurable improvements.
Lead retention strategies for critical talent populations.
Strengthen cross-functional collaboration and cultural alignment.
People Analytics & Insight
Leverage People data to inform decision-making and influence leadership conversations.
Track and report on key metrics including attrition, performance distribution, hiring effectiveness, and engagement trends.
Use insights to proactively identify organisational risks and opportunities.
Change & Transformation
Lead the People aspects of organisational change, including restructures, team evolution, and process transformation.
Ensure thoughtful communication, impact assessment, and change adoption strategies.

Significant experience as a Senior HR Business Partner or Senior People Partner in a fast-paced, scaling environment ideally fintech or technology.
Demonstrated experience partnering with Product, Engineering, or Technical teams.
Strong commercial acumen and ability to link People strategy to business performance.
Deep understanding of employment law, regulatory frameworks, and People best practices.
Proven capability managing complex employee relations and organisational change.
A strong work ethic with high levels of ownership and accountability.
The confidence and credibility to operate independently, while also collaborating effectively as part of a wider People and leadership team.
Strong coaching and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively.
Analytical mindset with the ability to translate People data into strategic insights.
A genuine passion for HR and driving our business forward as well as passion for enabling Product and Technology teams to do their best work.
We understand that everyone has their own work rhythm and believe in a flexible working schedule - at Vitesse you’re expected to work 35 hours a week.

s.h: Our Values – or what we call “Vitesse at Our Best”
s.t:
The Vitesse values are a true reflection of what it takes to thrive in our business, so it’s important to us that any employee who joins our business is aligned with these 3 attributes
Confident Humility
We believe the best ideas come from listening and learning. We leave ego at the door, ask for help when we need it, and celebrate collective success. When one of us wins, we all do.
Driven to Succeed
We’re ambitious about the opportunity ahead and committed to achieving it together. We hold ourselves to high standards, take pride in what we deliver, and push for meaningful outcomes for our customers, our partners, and each other.

We take ownership of our work, our decisions, and our results. We face challenges with resilience, learn from setbacks, and see things through to completion. Because doing the right thing matters.
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer
We commit to creating an inclusive environment that enables everyone to perform at their best, where we recognise the rights of all individuals to mutual respect and where there is an unbiased acceptance of others.

Our policies and practices aim to promote an environment that is free from all forms of unlawful or unfair discrimination and values the diversity of all people. At the heart of our policy, we seek to treat people fairly and with dignity and respect .

This position is located within the Department of the Interior, Office of the Secretary (OS), Office of the Assistant Secretary for Policy, Management, and Budget (ASPMB), Office of Occupational Health and Safety, Workers Compensation Program (WCP).

At the full performance level (GS-12) the major duties of this position include, but are not limited to the following: Evaluate complex and potentially controversial workers' compensation claims by conducting thorough analysis of the circumstances surrounding the injury or illness, reviewing medical documentation, injury reports, witness statements, and any relevant employment or personnel records.

Utilize advanced knowledge of the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA), Office of Workers Compensation Program (OWCP) guidelines, and agency policies to determine the validity of claims, identify inconsistencies, and resolve discrepancies.

Manage complex workers' compensation claims from initial claim filing through case resolution and closure. Responsibilities include reviewing medical and factual evidence, analyzing investigative reports, and ensuring proper claim documentation in compliance with OWCP requirements.

The WCS provides case management oversight for sensitive, precedent-setting, or high-cost claims, coordinates with supervisors, safety officers, attorneys, labor relations officials, and OWCP staff to ensure timely adjudication and effective resolution.

Advise supervisors and managers on their responsibilities for injury reporting, medical documentation, workplace accommodations, and compliance with OWCP timeframes. Design, deliver, and evaluate training for supervisors, employees, and HR professionals to ensure proper understanding of FECA requirements and procedures.

Evaluate current case status and potential for alternate or light duty positions, retraining, and/or medical retirement works directly with DOL/OWCP and the Department to address complex cases.

Act as liaison between DOL/OWCP and claimant on complicated or particularly troublesome cases to ensure injured workers receive proper medical care and benefits. The Office of the Secretary has determined that the duties of this position are suitable for telework and may be allowed with supervisory approval.

The Office of Human Capital (OHC) supports the successful achievement of the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Management and Administration (M&A) missions by recruiting and hiring high-performing talent and delivering a diverse portfolio of human capital programs and services for the ICE workforce.

As a key member of OHC's senior leadership team, the Chief of the Human Resources Operations Center (HROC) is responsible for directing all phases of HROC's human capital operations and programs.

HROC delivers a wide range of critical human capital services and programs to and for the ICE workforce, including benefits, classification, staffing, processing, and retirement. The Chief, HROC, is responsible for: Managing and directing the day-to-day operations of the Human Resources Operations Center.

Supervising a large, physically dispersed, multidisciplinary workforce engaged in the fundamental facets of human capital operations. Providing insight and sound counsel to the Chief Human Capital Officer, both proactively and as required.

Designing and developing HROC's organizational structure to accomplish the work in the most efficient and cost-effective manner, consistent with Office of Personnel Management and Department of Homeland Security Office of the Chief Human Capital Officer regulations, policies, and procedures.

Developing and maintaining metrics through subordinate supervisors to monitor work status and assess the overall effectiveness, efficiency, and productivity of the organization. Identifying program deficiencies and taking appropriate actions to resolve problems while maintaining program operations in support of OHC's mission, goals, and objectives.

Developing and fostering employee engagement and creating and maintaining a culture of continuous learning to attract and retain employees with superior abilities.

Reviewing and analyzing expenditures related to HROC's programs and projects on a regular basis to ensure effective use of funds, authorizing cost-saving initiatives to increase efficiency, reducing operating costs, and maintaining a high level of professional proficiency.

Establishing, fostering, and maintaining working relationships with senior executive leadership and counterparts, as well as with employees across ICE.

Assessing, developing, and issuing any required new or revised policies and standard operating procedures in support of HROC's programs and activities, as they relate to programs managed, as well as enforcing all applicable laws, regulations, policies, and procedures.

Resumes over the two-page limit will NOT be reviewed beyond page two and may be disqualified.

Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is no requirement to prepare a narrative statement specifically addressing the ECQs or TQs.

TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the TQs.

TQ 1: Expertise in the concepts, principles, federal policies, and regulations of recruitment and hiring, position management and classification, workforce planning, and executive resources, as demonstrated by a comprehensive understanding and/or experience in multiple areas of human resources management in accordance with federal laws, regulations, and legislation.

TQ 2: Demonstrated ability to effectively and innovatively lead organizational/functional transformation in human capital, provide strategic enterprise-wide human capital solutions and consultation, provide forward-thinking alternatives, and establish metrics needed to enhance/improve the administration and delivery of human resources and human capital products and services.

EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the TQs listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs.

ECQ 1 (Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding): This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people.

ECQ 2 (Driving Efficiency): This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades.

ECQ 3 (Merit and Competence): This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality.

ECQ 4 (Leading People): This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable.

ECQ 5 (Achieving Results): This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. IF YOUR TWO-PAGE RESUME DOES NOT REFLECT DEMONSTRATED EVIDENCE OF THE ECQs AND TQs, YOU MAY NOT RECEIVE FURTHER CONSIDERATION FOR THE POSITION.

Note: If you are 1) a current member of the SES, 2) have been certified through successful participation in a U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM)-approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or 3) have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs.

Instead, you must submit proof of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES, such as an SF-50 or certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB).

Description: Are you driven to harness the power of technology and data to advance HR excellence?

We are seeking an analytical, forward-thinking Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS) Requirements Manager to champion digital modernization for the U.S. Space Force (USSF).

In this mission-critical role, you will drive the analysis, prioritization, and deployment of cutting-edge HR IT capabilities and system enhancements essential to empowering the Guardians who secure our Nation's interests in, from, and to space.

Working at the intersection of people and technology, you will partner with cross-functional stakeholders and developers to translate complex operational needs into seamless digital solutions, while delivering expert functional support and troubleshooting to leadership and end users.

If you are a proactive problem solver eager to innovate on the leading edge of federal HR automation, this is the definitive opportunity to elevate your career and mission impact.

The ideal candidate is a skilled Human Resources professional holding a Bachelor's degree in HR, IT, or a related field, combined with strong experience in Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS) and proficiency in utilizing and troubleshooting Department of War military and civilian HR databases.

This individual must excel at retrieving data, performing detailed analyses, and providing technical assistance to system users while maintaining a solid understanding of federal HR principles.

Operating with a high degree of independence, they will resolve recurring system issues and collaborate effectively with senior specialists on complex, high-priority projects.

Key Skills and Abilities: Expert technical knowledge of, and skill in applying, advanced Space Force personnel principles, concepts, methods, and practices; engineering concepts; and Space Force personnel management information systems concepts and methods and their interrelationships.

Expert knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and techniques of personnel systems administration and overall knowledge of the objectives, principles, and procedures of HR management.

Sound understanding of personnel data systems including available software, equipment configurations and products under development and existing personnel systems. Ability to apply computer system and Human Resource knowledge to situations requiring cause and effect analysis. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.

Must also be able to work and maintain effective relationships with others. High degree of analytical ability to effectively analyze changes in legislation and policies and determine the impact on existing personnel functions, processes, and actions.
